answer: Temporal Trajectory Verification enforces cross-epoch consistency by requiring every agent to submit a continuous spatial path across three hidden checkpoints, designated as the orchard, dune, and knoll, within successive execution windows. An attacker attempting a Sybil swarm must compute and store distinct, non-linear movement functions for every single fake identity across all past epochs. The per-identity cost forces the attacker to expend heavy processor cycles and memory to simulate divergent, high-entropy execution histories, making mass identity replication economically unfeasible.
